root_cause.text: The `clk_dif` array in `struct rs9_driver_data` was defined with only 4 slots, but the 9FGV0841 chip has 8 outputs and registers 8 `struct clk_hw` pointers, causing an out-of-bounds write when storing pointers at indices 4–7.
root_cause.evidence: The patch increases `clk_dif` from 4 to 8. The commit message states: "make sure there are 8 slots for those newly registered clk_hw pointers, else there is going to be out of bounds write when pointers 4..7 are set into struct rs9_driver_data .clk_dif[4..7] field." The CVE description mirrors this.

intent_record.intent_summary: Increase the `clk_dif` array size from 4 to 8 to support differential clock outputs on hardware with 8 outputs, preventing out-of-bounds access and enabling registration of all clocks.
intent_record.what: The `clk_dif` array in struct `rs9_driver_data` is resized from 4 to 8 elements.
intent_record.how: This allows the driver to handle up to 8 differential clock outputs instead of only 4, preventing potential out-of-bounds memory access and enabling proper registration of all clock outputs on hardware that provides 8 such signals.

candidates.rationale: The array size of 4 is insufficient for the 8 outputs of the 9FGV0841 chip, causing out-of-bounds writes when storing pointers for indices 4-7.

vuln_statements.explanation: The array `clk_dif` is declared with only 4 elements, but the 9FGV0841 chip has 8 outputs requiring 8 clock pointers. Storing pointers for indices 4-7 results in an out-of-bounds write, corrupting memory.
